name: ACCORD, ACcurate COnsensus Reporting Document (consensus methods)
citation: Gattrell WT, Logullo P, van Zuuren EJ, Price A, Hughes EL, Blazey P, et al. ACCORD (ACcurate COnsensus Reporting Document): a reporting guideline for consensus methods in biomedicine developed via a modified Delphi. PLoS Med 2024;21(1):e1004326. The final checklist (Table 4) labels its 35 items by section (T1, I1-I3, M1-M21, R1-R5, D1-D2, O1-O3); they are numbered 1-35 here in that order and each topic starts with the checklist's code. It covers Delphi, nominal group, RAND/UCLA and other consensus methods. See https://www.equator-network.org/reporting-guidelines/accord/

items.topic: T1 Title names a consensus exercise and method
items.question: Does the title identify the report as a consensus exercise and name the method used (for example Delphi or nominal group)?
Does the introduction explain why a consensus exercise was chosen rather than another approach?
Are the aim of the exercise, its intended audience and its geographical scope stated?

items.topic: I3 Update of an earlier document
items.question: If the exercise updates an existing document, is the reason for the update given and the original cited?
Is the registration of the study or its protocol reported with the platform and a link, or its absence stated?
Are the roles and expertise of those directing the exercise (chair, steering committee, subgroups) described, with how they were chosen?

items.topic: M3 Panel inclusion criteria and size
items.question: Are the criteria for including panellists and the rationale for the panel's size explained, with who selected them?
Is the recruitment of panellists described: how they were invited, how many invitations were sent and whether they could suggest others?

items.topic: M5 Public, patient and carer involvement
items.question: Is the role of members of the public, patients or carers at each step described, or their absence stated?
Is it described how information was gathered before the items or materials were drafted (literature review, interviews, surveys)?
If a systematic search was run, is it described in detail (strategy and dates) or is its published report cited?

items.topic: M8 Evidence summary given to the panel
items.question: Is it described how existing evidence was summarised and whether that summary was given to the panellists?
Are the consensus method and its steps described, with any modification of the method explained and justified?
Are the way each statement was presented, the response options and whether panellists could comment or add items described?
Is the objective of each consensus step (round, meeting or discussion) stated?
Is the definition of consensus (a threshold or rating) stated with the rationale for it?

items.topic: M13 Items carried into later rounds
items.question: Does the report say whether items that had already reached consensus were put to later voting rounds?
Is it described, for each step, how responses were collected and whether individually or in a group?

items.topic: M15 Processing and synthesis of responses
items.question: Is it described how responses were processed or synthesised, including any analysis of free-text comments?
Is any piloting of the materials described (who, how many, what changed, whether pilot answers counted), or its absence stated?
Is the feedback given to panellists after each step described: quantitative or qualitative, and whether anonymised?
Is it stated whether anonymity was planned, to whom it applied and how it was protected?

items.topic: M19 Steering committee's part in decisions
items.question: Does the report say whether the steering committee took part in the panel's decisions or voted?
Are any incentives or reminders used to encourage participation described?
Are adaptations that made the surveys or meetings accessible (languages, translations, plain-language summaries) described?
Are the start date and the time each consensus step and its analysis took reported, with any delays?
Are deviations from the protocol (panel changes, number of steps, stopping rules) reported with their reasons and the step affected?
Are the number of panellists, the response rate and relevant panel characteristics reported for each step?

items.topic: R4 Final outcome of the consensus
items.question: Is the final outcome reported as qualitative themes and/or quantitative summaries (for example medians or ranges) of agreement?
Are the items or topics modified or dropped during the process listed, with when and why?

items.topic: D1 Strengths and limitations of the method
items.question: Are the exercise's methodological strengths and limitations discussed, including response rates, panel representativeness and possible bias from feedback?
Is it discussed whether the recommendations agree with earlier literature, and why they may differ where they do not?
Are any endorsing organisations named with their role?
Are potential conflicts of interest of the organisers and panellists declared, with how they were managed?

items.topic: O3 Funding and the funder's role
items.question: Is the funding stated with the funder's role in design, the steering committee, the consensus process and any writing support?
